title.en: Fit Body, Fit Mind, Fit Nation

text.en: A rhyming poem introduces cheerful children: Anant the hockey player, Geeta the skater, Lhamo and his guitar, Shabana the cyclist and Meena who sings in rhythm. Each child is described with a word that starts with the same letter as their name. In this chapter you will read the poem, learn describing words (adjectives), find rhymes and double letters, and learn about the Paralympic Games.

The poem introduces children who enjoy sports and music, each with a describing word before their name. Active Anant plays hockey even when the ground is rocky. Graceful Geeta skates and learns every day from her mistakes. Little Lhamo proudly plays the guitar while his friend plays the sitar. Swift Shabana celebrates after winning a cycle race at her fastest pace. Musical Meena sings in rhythm, and cheerful children everywhere find playing a joy. The title says that a fit body, a fit mind and a fit nation go together: when children play and stay healthy, the whole country grows strong.
Games and exercise keep our body strong and our mind alert. Music and dance help us move in rhythm and feel happy. Learning from mistakes, as Geeta does, helps us improve every day. You can ask yourself which game you like and whether you enjoy indoor or outdoor games more.
Mistakes are things done wrongly. Proudly means with a feeling of pride. Pace is the speed at which we move. Rhythm is a regular beat in music or movement. Cheerful means happy. Swift means very fast.
A word that tells more about a noun is called an adjective. Blue sky, hardworking children, green leaves, pebbled road and healthy vegetables are examples. Happy child, red apple, fierce lion and beautiful flower show how an adjective goes before the noun. You can add your own: sweet mangoes, cute baby, proud nation and clever winner.
Rhyming words have the same ending sound. Hockey and rocky rhyme. Skates and mistakes rhyme. Guitar rhymes with sitar. Race rhymes with pace. Joy rhymes with boy. Some words have a double letter, like village, ball, carrot, apple, kitchen and butter.
Proudly means feeling happy about something you did well. Brave means courageous and bold. Rocky means uneven or full of difficulties. Delightful means very pleasing or enjoyable. Mistakes are errors, or things done incorrectly.
The Paralympic Games are an international sports event for athletes with physical disabilities. They show that determination and practice matter more than anything, and they are held after the Olympic Games. Find out about Indian Paralympic athletes and share what you learn with the class. You can also try Preparing a Dish Without Fire, such as a fruit salad or a sandwich, with your teacher's help.
Let us think about the poem. Each child is described with a word that starts with the same letter as the name, like active Anant and graceful Geeta. Write one quality for your own name that starts with the same letter, such as smart Sana or brave Bilal. Think and discuss: which game do you play in school, and do you enjoy indoor games or outdoor games more? Name a musical instrument you like and a famous dance from your region, and tell your friends how it is played or performed.

problem.en: Pick the adjective: The healthy vegetables are green.

text.en: An adjective tells more about a noun.
Healthy and green describe the vegetables.

why.en: They tell how the vegetables are.

text.en: So healthy and green are adjectives.
Rocky ends with the sound ocky.
Hockey has the same ending.
So the rhyme is hockey.

prompt.en: Explain what the poem says about children and why a fit body helps a fit nation.

requiredIdeas.en: Healthy children make a strong nation

points.en: Children in the poem enjoy hockey, skating, cycling, music and singing.
An adjective tells more about a noun.
Rhyming words end with the same sound.
Paralympic Games are for athletes with disabilities.
A fit body and mind make a fit nation.
